question: Solve the equation \(\frac{x}{x-3}=2-\frac{1}{3-x}\).
solution: On the right-hand side, \(-\frac{1}{3-x}=\frac{1}{x-3}\). Multiplying both sides by \(x-3\) gives \(x=2(x-3)+1\), so \(x=5\). Checking gives \(x-3\ne0\), so \(x=5\).
